FROM ops.zones z
WHERE z.LocationID NOT IN (SELECT t.RatecodeID FROM lake.trips t WHERE t.PULocationID = z.LocationID)
ORDER BY z.LocationID

diagnosis.bottleneck: The NOT IN subquery is evaluated as a correlated left-delimited join that forces a full scan of 495,833 trips rows for each of the 265 zones, and the inner hash join builds a large hash table on the correlated RatecodeID values before probing.

hypotheses.claim: NOT IN over a subquery forces a null-aware anti join, which is expensive. (matched: not in (select t.ratecodeid from lake.trips t where t.pulocationid = z.locationid) order b)

The LEFT_DELIM_JOIN implements NOT IN with correlated subquery semantics, causing repeated execution of the inner pipeline per zones row; rewriting to NOT EXISTS or a LEFT ANTI JOIN would allow a single scan of trips and a single hash build.

The inner HASH_JOIN builds a hash table on the correlated RatecodeID values (estimated 167 distinct) and probes 495,833 trips rows; if RatecodeID has many NULLs the NOT IN semantics force extra null-aware checks that inflate CPU.

The SEQ_SCAN on trips reads all 495,833 rows without predicate pushdown because PULocationID = z.LocationID is a correlation reference; adding an index on trips(PULocationID) or materializing distinct RatecodeID per PULocationID would let the engine avoid the full scan.
